$comment: Source of truth for the pack. Every skill folder under skills/ has an entry here and the SKILL.md frontmatter must match it (node tools/validate.mjs). status: beta (tested and method-reviewed) -> stable.

handoffs.H: To field this, connect the QuestionPunk MCP server (https://app.questionpunk.com/api/v1, OAuth sign-in).
handoffs.H-adv: MaxDiff, conjoint, Kano, Gabor-Granger and Van Westendorp are QuestionPunk question types; some can only be created in the app, not over MCP.

plugins.survey-design: Design, check, size and recruit for questionnaires before they go out.
plugins.pricing-research: Van Westendorp, Gabor-Granger, MaxDiff and conjoint: design and analysis.
plugins.feedback-analysis: Clean, weight, code and analyze survey answers: NPS, CSAT/CES, PMF, Likert, Kano, UX scales, crosstabs, open ends.
plugins.interviews: Interview guides for AI-moderated customer and user interviews.

skills.name: survey-bias-check
skills.title: Survey bias check
skills.description: Reviews a survey or questionnaire for question wording and design problems: leading, loaded, double-barreled, assumptive and hypothetical questions, double negatives, unbalanced scales, overlapping or gapped answer ranges, missing "none" or "other" options, recall periods, agree/disagree grids and length, with a rewrite for each problem question. Use for checking, auditing or linting survey questions, a feedback form, an NPS or CSAT survey, a Google Form, Typeform or Qualtrics draft, or pasted questions before launch, or for "what is wrong with my survey".

skills.name: survey-from-decision
skills.title: Survey from a decision
skills.description: Designs a survey backward from the decision it informs: decision rule, hypotheses, each question with its reason, the analysis plan with empty result tables, target sample and estimated length. Use for survey design: "write a survey", "design a survey", "survey questions for X", "customer feedback survey", "questionnaire for X", "feedback form", or a CSAT, CES, NPS, in-app, post-purchase, employee pulse or event feedback survey. Not for reviewing an existing survey (that is survey-bias-check).

skills.name: qsf-convert
skills.title: QSF convert
skills.handoff: QuestionPunk imports .qsf, PDF and Word questionnaires in the app, where AI follow-ups can be added to open questions.
skills.description: Converts a survey written in Markdown (or pasted from a doc or form) into a Qualtrics import file: a .qsf with blocks, question types, skip and display logic, or Advanced Format TXT when there is no logic. Also turns an exported .qsf into editable Markdown or a codebook with a list of what could not be carried, and checks a .qsf for broken references. Use for "make this a Qualtrics survey", "import my survey into Qualtrics", "read this qsf", "check this qsf", "Qualtrics data dictionary" or "move my survey between tools".

skills.name: open-ended-coding
skills.title: Open-ended coding
skills.description: Builds a codebook from open-ended survey answers, applies it to every row of a CSV with a definition for every code, counts themes with honest denominators, pulls verbatim quotes with row ids, and checks coder agreement (Cohen's kappa, Krippendorff's alpha) on a double-coded sample, human or LLM. Use for "code these responses", "themes from open-ended answers", "thematic analysis of survey comments", "categorize or tag free-text feedback", "analyze NPS comments or verbatims", "inter-rater reliability" or "does the LLM coding agree with mine".

skills.name: nps-analysis
skills.title: NPS analysis
skills.description: Computes Net Promoter Score (NPS) with its confidence interval (margin of error) from raw 0-10 scores or promoter, passive and detractor counts, tests differences between segments, periods or against a target, and splits comments by promoter, passive and detractor so the reasons can be coded and counted. Use for "analyze our NPS", "calculate NPS from this export", "why did NPS drop", "is the NPS change significant", "NPS by segment", "what are detractors saying" or eNPS results.

skills.name: pmf-survey
skills.title: PMF survey
skills.description: Designs, scores and segments a Sean Ellis product-market-fit survey (the 40% "very disappointed" test): exact questions, who to sample, the score with a confidence interval and a stated N/A rule, segment scores, and the Superhuman (Rahul Vohra) engine for finding must-have users, what they value and what holds the rest back. Use for "do we have PMF", "measure product-market fit", "PMF survey", "Sean Ellis test", "40% rule", "very disappointed score", "did our PMF score change" or "Superhuman PMF engine".

skills.name: van-westendorp-analysis
skills.title: Van Westendorp analysis
skills.description: Computes a Van Westendorp price sensitivity meter (PSM) from a CSV of survey answers: optimal (OPP) and indifference (IPP/IDP) price points, PMC, PME and the acceptable price range, plus the optional Newton-Miller-Smith purchase-intent extension. Flags inconsistent respondents and prints the convention used, so results can be compared with R, Conjointly or Sawtooth. Use for "Van Westendorp", "price sensitivity meter", "PSM analysis", "acceptable price range", "willingness to pay survey" or "what should we charge" when you have four-question pricing survey data.

skills.name: maxdiff-design
skills.title: MaxDiff design
skills.description: Builds or checks a balanced MaxDiff (best-worst scaling) experimental design: items per set, sets per respondent and versions, exact BIBDs from cyclic, affine-plane and complete constructions or a balanced search otherwise, with checks on item frequency, pair frequency, position balance and connectivity, plus respondent-facing question wording. Use for "MaxDiff study", "best-worst scaling", "feature prioritization survey", "which features matter most", "rank messages or claims", "how many MaxDiff sets" or "check my MaxDiff design".

skills.name: maxdiff-analysis
skills.title: MaxDiff analysis
skills.description: Scores MaxDiff (best-worst scaling, BWS) results from a CSV: counting scores and an aggregate multinomial logit, giving utilities and preference shares with bootstrap intervals, model fit and segment comparisons. Use for "analyze MaxDiff", "best-worst scores", "share of preference", "which features matter most" or "feature priority results" from a Sawtooth, Qualtrics or other survey export. Not for building the design (maxdiff-design) or individual-level HB utilities.

skills.name: survey-sample-size
skills.title: Survey sample size
skills.handoff: QuestionPunk can quote a Prolific panel and count eligible participants without charging.
skills.description: Calculates survey sample size: how many responses are needed for a margin of error and confidence level, a power analysis to compare two groups (minimum detectable difference), NPS margins and comparisons, minimum subgroup sizes, MaxDiff and conjoint rules of thumb, invitations from a response rate, and how many interviews reach saturation. Use for "how many people do I need", "what's the margin of error on 150 responses", "is n=80 enough" or "is my sample big enough to be statistically significant".

skills.name: ai-interview-guide
skills.title: AI interview guide
skills.handoff: Run it as a text or voice AI interview in QuestionPunk.
skills.description: Turns research goals or an existing discussion guide or interview script into a brief an AI moderator can run for customer or user research: goal, must-ask questions, probes and probe depth, skip rules, topics to avoid, a consent screen with AI disclosure and a short opener, length, and a paste-ready interviewer prompt, with leading questions rewritten. Use for "interview 30 customers", "async user interviews", "AI-moderated interviews", "write the prompt for my AI interviewer" or "run my discussion guide at scale".

skills.name: survey-data-cleaning
skills.title: Survey data cleaning
skills.handoff: QuestionPunk flags suspected fraud; filter it with suspiciousLevel.
skills.description: Screens a survey export for response quality: flags speeders, straight-liners, duplicates, failed attention checks, gibberish or copy-pasted open answers, inconsistent answers and platform bot or fraud flags. Writes a flags file and a cleaning log, removes rows only by a rule the user approves, and never changes the original. Use for "clean this survey data", "remove bad responses, bots or speeders", "careless responding", "which responses should I drop" or before analyzing any survey CSV (Qualtrics, Google Forms or other exports).

skills.name: csat-ces-analysis
skills.title: CSAT and CES analysis
skills.description: Computes CSAT and Customer Effort Score (CES) from ratings or counts: the top-2-box share with a Wilson interval and the mean, CES on the 7-point agree or ease scale or the original 1-5 effort scale (lower is better), with the convention printed so numbers reconcile with Zendesk or Qualtrics; tests differences between agents, channels, segments or periods and against a target; and splits comments by satisfied, neutral and dissatisfied. Use for "calculate CSAT", "CSAT from this export", "customer effort score", "CES results", "is our CSAT drop significant" or post-ticket surveys.

skills.name: survey-crosstabs
skills.title: Survey crosstabs
skills.description: Builds crosstabs (banner tables) from a survey CSV: column percentages with bases, significance letters from column-proportion tests with Holm or Benjamini-Hochberg correction, chi-square, intervals, weighted bases with Kish effective n, and an anonymity rule that hides groups and cells under k respondents. Use for "crosstab this survey", "banner table", "break results down by segment", "is this difference between groups real", "significance testing on survey results" or employee survey results by team.

skills.name: likert-analysis
skills.title: Likert analysis
skills.description: Analyzes Likert and other rating-scale items from a CSV: full distributions, top-2 and bottom-2 box with Wilson intervals, medians and means with guidance on which to lead with, a diverging stacked bar table, reverse-coded item detection, Cronbach's alpha with a Feldt interval and alpha-if-item-deleted, and group comparisons (Mann-Whitney per item, box differences, Welch t on the scale score). Use for "analyze Likert data", "agree/disagree results", "satisfaction scale results", "Cronbach's alpha", "is my scale reliable", "top-2-box" or "how should I report a 5-point scale".

skills.name: kano-analysis
skills.title: Kano analysis
skills.description: Designs and analyzes Kano surveys: writes the functional and dysfunctional question pair for each feature, classifies every answer with Kano's evaluation table (attractive, one-dimensional, must-be, indifferent, reverse, questionable), assigns each feature its category with Fong's test for a clear winner, and computes Better/Worse coefficients with intervals for a quadrant chart. Use for "Kano model", "Kano survey", "Kano analysis", "which features are must-haves vs delighters", "feature prioritization survey" or "better worse coefficients".

skills.name: conjoint-design
skills.title: Conjoint design
skills.description: Designs a choice-based conjoint (CBC) study: attributes and levels that don't overlap, prohibited combinations, tasks, concepts per task and a none option, a randomized design with level balance and minimal overlap (or fully randomized for AMCEs) generated by script, checks of level frequency, attribute association and relative D-efficiency, and a sample size from the Johnson-Orme rule. Use for "conjoint study", "design a conjoint", "discrete choice experiment", "which feature bundle", "trade-off research", "CBC design", "how many conjoint tasks" or "check my conjoint design".

skills.name: conjoint-analysis
skills.title: Conjoint analysis
skills.description: Analyzes choice-based conjoint results from a CSV of tasks and choices: an aggregate multinomial logit with respondent-clustered standard errors, part-worth utilities, attribute importances, willingness to pay when price is an attribute, AMCEs and marginal means for fully randomized designs, segment comparisons, and a share-of-preference simulator, with bootstrap intervals. Use for "analyze conjoint results", "part-worths", "attribute importance", "willingness to pay from conjoint", "market simulator" or a Sawtooth, Qualtrics or Conjointly CBC export. Not for individual-level HB utilities.

skills.name: ux-scale-scoring
skills.title: UX scale scoring
skills.description: Scores standard usability questionnaires from a CSV: SUS (0-100, standard or all-positive wording, with checks for miscoded data), UMUX-Lite (raw, read on the SUS grades, plus the historical SUS-equivalent), SEQ and raw NASA-TLX, with confidence intervals, the SUS curved grade, percentile and adjective from published benchmarks, and tests of two designs (independent or paired) or against a target such as 68. Use for "SUS score", "System Usability Scale results", "calculate SUS", "UMUX-Lite", "single ease question", "NASA-TLX", "usability questionnaire results" or "is our SUS above average".

skills.name: gabor-granger-analysis
skills.title: Gabor-Granger analysis
skills.description: Estimates a demand curve and the revenue- or profit-maximizing price from Gabor-Granger purchase-likelihood answers: take rate at each tested price with confidence intervals, a monotonicity check per respondent, a monotone demand curve, arc price elasticity, revenue and profit curves with a bootstrap check on the optimal price, and optional user-supplied weights for stated-intent overclaim. Reads full, adaptive or monadic price ladders. Use for "Gabor-Granger", "price ladder results", "demand curve from survey", "revenue-maximizing price", "price test results" or "would you buy at $X" data.

skills.name: survey-weighting
skills.title: Survey weighting
skills.description: Weights a survey sample to known population totals by raking (iterative proportional fitting) or cell weighting: reads target margins, rakes to a stated tolerance, trims extreme weights and re-rakes, and reports the design effect, Kish effective sample size, weight distribution and weighted estimates, writing a new file and never overwriting the data. Also reports the design effect of existing weights. Use for "weight my survey", "raking", "rim weighting", "rake to census", "post-stratification", "my sample has too many women or young people", "design effect" or "effective sample size".

skills.name: screener-writer
skills.title: Screener writer
skills.description: Turns a target participant profile into a recruiting screener: behavioral qualifying questions with decoy options so the right answer can't be guessed, terminate and quota logic, an articulation question for interviews, and a script check that every route that qualifies passes a question for each profile criterion, every option routes, no question or option reveals the target, and quotas can fill. Use for "write a screener", "screener survey", "screener questions for user interviews", "recruit the right participants", "check my screener" or "qualify panel respondents".
